summary: Implemented the rootless buildkitd lifecycle in src/platform/buildkit.ts with ensure, status, and stop behind an injectable argument-array process runner; cold start uses the exact spike flags, reuses a healthy daemon, removes stale sockets, distinguishes name/socket conflicts, and enforces finite readiness and command timeouts. Added 21 unit tests using a recording fake runner and real temporary unix sockets; typecheck, lint, focused tests (21), full unit suite (333), and build all pass.

decisions: Container identity is easy-host-buildkitd with io.easy-host.role=buildkit; a container using that name without the label is foreign and is never removed, and a live socket without the managed container is a conflict rather than an adopted daemon.
Cold-start readiness is bounded at 20s with 100ms probes and a 1s probe timeout; podman run has a 600s budget for the cold image pull, inspect 15s, stop/rm 30s.

Lifecycle errors are PrerequisiteError exit 2 (socket timeout, start failure, podman missing, state unwritable) and ConflictError exit 6 (name/socket collision); BLD-1.3 remains responsible for mapping an unreachable daemon to build infrastructure-failure exit 3.
No --restart flag is added: the task requires flags to match the spike record exactly, and the spike command has no restart policy.
The shared platform runner does not exist yet, so buildkit.ts exposes a structurally compatible BuildkitRunner seam and ships a shell-free spawnSync default that can be replaced by injection.

payload.taskDescription: Implement buildkit.ts using the flags recorded by the spike. Provide ensure(): return an existing healthy daemon if its socket accepts a connection, otherwise start the pinned image with a named container, the state root mounted for socket and cache, and a finite readiness timeout. Provide stop() and status(). All podman calls go through the shared process runner with argument arrays. Tests use a recording fake runner and a temporary unix socket to cover reuse, cold start, readiness timeout, port or socket collision, and a failed start.
